Start year.note:
Start year of the gas conversion.

Newest Alliant statement:
- Open the Alliant Energy quarterly report for the period ended September 30, 2026 at https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/52485/000035254126000047/lnt-20260930.htm and search for 'Edgewater Unit 5'. The bullet that starts 'WPL currently plans to continue coal operations at Edgewater Unit 5 (414 MW)' says coal operations continue 'at least through 2030'. WPL is Wisconsin Power and Light Company.
- The unit therefore cannot be on gas before 2030, so 2030 stays. The human adds this as a new scheduled event with Event Year 2030 and Source Year 2026, and does not change an existing one.

Older dates:
- The Alliant press release from May 23, 2024 at https://s201.q4cdn.com/991130938/files/doc_news/2024/May/23/2024-5-23-nr-edgewater-fuel-switch.pdf set the conversion for 2028.
- An Urban Milwaukee article from June 5, 2026 at https://urbanmilwaukee.com/2026/06/05/trumps-425-million-coal-push-could-impact-wisconsin/ says Edgewater is 'slated to transition to natural gas generation by 2029'. It is a news story, not an Alliant filing, and is older than the November 2026 report.

The open comment thread on the start year can be closed with 2030.

Conversion/replacement?.note: The Alliant Energy press release from May 23, 2024 at https://s201.q4cdn.com/991130938/files/doc_news/2024/May/23/2024-5-23-nr-edgewater-fuel-switch.pdf says on page 1, in the first paragraph, that Alliant plans 'to convert its coal-fueled Edgewater Generating Station to natural gas'. That is a conversion.

Fuel.note: The same press release at https://s201.q4cdn.com/991130938/files/doc_news/2024/May/23/2024-5-23-nr-edgewater-fuel-switch.pdf names natural gas as the new fuel. It is a replacement for the Alliant news page that no longer opens.

Status.note:
Status stays announced for the gas conversion row.

Why:
- The EIA-860M table for September 2026 at https://www.eia.gov/electricity/data/eia860m/xls/september_generator2026.xlsx (sheet Operating, plant 4050, generator 5) lists 413.7 MW of conventional steam coal, operating since 1985, with Planned Repower Year 2028 and month 12. That row is the existing coal unit. This GEM row is the future gas conversion, so operating coal is not a conflict.
- The Alliant report at https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/52485/000035254126000047/lnt-20260930.htm says coal operations continue at least through 2030, so the conversion has not started.

No status change is proposed.
